findings.title: Security-motivated overload change lacks explanatory comment
findings.description: The only behavioral difference in this hunk is the static type of the argument passed to parseArray: componentType (Type) vs componentClass (Class<?>), which selects a different overload. This is the core of the CVE-2017-18349 fix, but nothing in the code explains why the Type overload must be avoided. Without a comment, a future maintainer may see the two variables as equivalent (since they are assigned from the same expression) and revert to componentType, reintroducing the vulnerability. Add a short comment referencing the security rationale.
evidence: ObjectArrayCodec.java line 177: parser.parseArray(componentClass, array, fieldName); replaces parser.parseArray(componentType, array, fieldName); with no comment
ObjectArrayCodec.java line 174: componentType = componentClass = clazz.getComponentType(); makes the two variables appear interchangeable, obscuring why componentClass is required.

rejections.reason: evidence verification rejected the candidate: The cited evidence does not establish that componentType and componentClass ever diverge. The visible diff hunk shows both assigned together as 'componentType = componentClass = clazz.getComponentType()', and there is no evidence in the available context of another branch where componentType is a ParameterizedType while componentClass is raw. The finding explicitly relies on code not visible in the diff, which violates the No Evidence, No Finding policy; it is speculative rather than evidence-backed.
